key_insight: Dynamically selecting measurement latency from the remaining error budget and QEC rounds can shorten logical cycles while reducing logical errors.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing measurements for logical performance rather than per-qubit readout fidelity can accelerate fault-tolerant quantum programs.
method: Use measurement latencies that balance logical cycle time and logical error rate.
Track the remaining error budget and QEC rounds within each logical cycle.
Select the fastest suitable latency for the upcoming round using a lightweight real-time policy.
evidence_signal: Evaluations report 1.69× average logical-cycle speedup, reaching 2.29×, with logical error rates averaging 0.46× baseline and reaching as low as 0.13×.
watch_item: Deployment requires timely runtime error information and measurement-latency control; the abstract does not specify hardware validation or controller overhead.
paper_title: DynaMite: Dynamic Measurement Scheduling To Accelerate Fault-Tolerant Quantum Programs
